DEFER (revisitable): thread/rollback irreversibly drops the last N turns in place, is lossy, and does NOT revert the agent's file changes (transcript/working-tree divergence). Fork covers the safe non-destructive 'go back' case. Revisit requires content-derived revision machinery, a file-revert/divergence story, T1-only gating, and an explicit destructive-confirm UX. See docs/project/roadmap.md.
app-server account login / credential entry is an R3 trust-boundary action not exposed to remote clients (parallels opencode /connect)

Claude channel true-sync (--channels MCP bridge) is architecturally dead: claude.ai only honors permission replies from channels on Anthropic's curated allowlist, so the channel can display but not control. Reviewed out until Anthropic allowlists it; Claude sync stays Observe + Drive + PreToolUse hooks.

Issue 15a (2026-08-19): Drive never forks. A forked resume writes a second branch on the shared transcript tree that the terminal owner cannot see, and the activity watcher and resume hints all had to re-point mid-flight. Takeover now resumes in place; a mid-turn terminal owner is refused at attach, and a later terminal write demotes the drive to observe.
